summary: Telegram-controlled remote shell backdoor on installer host
details: httpz-requests ships a Telegram bot that, once started via the exported start_bot entry point, treats messages from Telegram users listed in an OWNERS array as commands to execute on the installer's machine. Supported operations include arbitrary shell execution (.sh <command>), Python code execution (.py), filesystem exfiltration via split-zip backups (take, get all), and destructive operations such as rm -rf. Commands are XOR+base64-encoded before being handed to `bash -c` via `echo <b64> | base64 -d | bash` to hide plaintext from process listings and shell logs, execution is disguised as HTTP calls, and the Telegram bot token itself is stored encoded and decoded at runtime by a shipped compiled module obfuscate.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so. The distribution name is near-collision with the httpx/requests ecosystem, and publisher metadata is placeholder (Author-email `Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, Homepage `https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`), reducing attribution. Whoever holds the bot token gains full remote code execution, file read/exfil, and destructive capability on any host that imports and starts this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
